title: What's cooking 🍳
intro: The tools I'm building and testing to take the grunt work out of analytics. Tap any one to see what it does and why it's worth having.

projects.name: GA4 audit
projects.summary: An automated health check of a Google Analytics 4 property that gives the same answer every time it runs.
does: Reads the property's set-up through Google's APIs: data streams, events, key events, custom definitions, data retention, consent and links like BigQuery and Google Ads
Checks each one against a fixed set of rules, so the result is deterministic rather than an opinion
Never touches personal data: it audits configuration, not people
Produces a scored report with what's wrong, why it matters and how to fix it
benefits: Hours of clicking through admin screens becomes a few minutes
Re-run it after changes and compare like with like
Catches gaps (missing key events, short retention, broken links) before they quietly cost months of data

projects.name: GTM audit + dataLayer generator, end to end
projects.summary: From 'what should we track?' to a tested Tag Manager container, with one source of truth the whole way through.
does: Audits an existing GTM container: tags, triggers, variables, naming, duplicates, unused items and consent settings
Turns a measurement plan into a dataLayer spec and ready-to-paste developer snippets
Generates an importable GTM container and a data dictionary that match the spec exactly
Keeps personal data out by design: hashing where it's needed, nothing raw in the dataLayer
benefits: Developers, analysts and marketers all work from the same spec
Days of hand-building tags drops to an import and a check
New tracking always traces back to a documented line, so audits stay easy

projects.name: Personal dashboard + automated data warehouse
projects.summary: My own data flowing into BigQuery on a schedule, with a dashboard that's always up to date.
does: Pulls data from the sources I use into BigQuery automatically
Cleans and models it with version-controlled SQL, so every number has a known definition
Feeds a dashboard that refreshes itself, with no manual exports
benefits: A working reference build for the same pattern at any scale
No more copy-paste reporting or stale screenshots
A safe sandbox for trying new tools (like the ones below) on real data

projects.name: Data Agent Kit experiments
projects.summary: Testing Google's new Data Agent Kit: coding agents that can query, build pipelines and do data science on BigQuery.
does: Connects a coding agent to BigQuery and other Google Cloud data services with Google's own skills and tools
Lets the agent write and tune SQL, build and fix pipelines, and run analysis from a plain-English request
Puts real guardrails in place first: an IAM policy that blocks write actions, rather than trusting the agent's 'ask before deleting' instruction
benefits: Finds out what's genuinely useful versus what's demo-only, before anyone relies on it
Builds a safe set-up pattern others can copy
Compares Google's approach with Snowflake, Databricks and Microsoft (see the October edition)

projects.name: Playwright tracking tests
projects.summary: A robot browser that clicks through a site and checks the tracking actually fired, in preview and in production.
does: Opens pages and runs the key journeys (page views, clicks, forms) like a real visitor
Watches network requests to see exactly which tags fired and what they sent
Inspects the dataLayer at each step against the spec
Reads the site's Content Security Policy and flags any vendor (Meta, Google Ads and others) it would block
benefits: Tests GTM changes in preview before they go live
Diagnoses production issues in minutes instead of guesswork
Catches silent breakages, like a site release that quietly kills a conversion tag

projects.name: Environmental scan automation
projects.summary: A monthly sweep of what changed in measurement, privacy and AI, with every item dated and linked to its source.
does: Searches a fixed window (the last month) across platforms, regulators, standards bodies and trusted practitioners
Filters out recycled stats and vendor fluff, keeping only what actually changed
Writes each item as what happened, why it matters and what to do about it
Publishes as a readable briefing, like On the Pulse
benefits: Staying current takes a read, not a day of searching
Every claim can be checked against its source
Turns news into a short list of actions

outro: Got a tool you'd like to see here, or want to compare notes? Leave a comment on the latest edition.
